# Guarded bidirectional sync runs end to end: first-run refusal, resync
# baseline, dry-run preview and propagation.
mkdir local
mkdir remote-files
exec sh -c 'printf "[nas]\ntype = alias\nremote = %s\n" "$1" > rclone.conf' sh $WORK/remote-files
chmod 0600 rclone.conf

exec sh -c 'printf "state: %s\nrclone_config: %s\n" "$1" "$2" > drivebridge.yaml' sh $WORK/state $WORK/rclone.conf

exec drivebridge space add --space nas --backend generic --remote nas --local-root $WORK/local --max-bytes 1048576
stdout 'Space configured'

# The first run without an explicit resync is refused; nothing changes.
exec sh -c 'printf hello > local/a.txt'
! exec drivebridge sync --space nas
stderr 'resync_required'
! exists $WORK/remote-files/a.txt

# --resync establishes the baseline and propagates both ways.
exec sh -c 'printf world > remote-files/b.txt'
exec drivebridge sync --space nas --resync --json
stdout '"status":"success"'
exists $WORK/remote-files/a.txt
exists $WORK/local/b.txt

# A dry run plans without touching either side.
exec sh -c 'printf pending > local/c.txt'
exec drivebridge sync --space nas --dry-run --json
stdout '"dry_run":true'
! exists $WORK/remote-files/c.txt

# The real run propagates the addition and registers stable references.
exec drivebridge sync --space nas --json
stdout '"status":"success"'
exists $WORK/remote-files/c.txt
exec drivebridge find --space nas --query c.txt --json
stdout '"count":1'

# Deletions above the tightened cap abort with the exact ratio; the explicit
# override is required to proceed.
exec sh -c 'rm local/a.txt local/b.txt'
! exec drivebridge sync --space nas
stderr 'sync_deletion_cap_exceeded'
exists $WORK/remote-files/a.txt
exec drivebridge sync --space nas --max-delete 100 --json
stdout '"status":"success"'
! exists $WORK/remote-files/a.txt
